cleared.check: Task 1 (lead L-867), strict rerun of the cycle 18 swaps on the 512 bit branch. Group set: every group of cycles/018/theme-hyperevm-v3-rest.work/out/rest-*.json.groups.jsonl whose counts hold branch:m512, 34,534 groups with 39,752 swaps (v3strict19.py). Each swap was run twice from parent-block state on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (web3_clientVersion reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 at 16:35:50 UTC, every 5,000 groups and at the end of each shard, last at 17:45:01 UTC on 2026-11-25). The lenient run repeats the cycle 18 rule and finds the 36,665 swaps with 104,643 calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv again, the same counts as cycle 18. The strict run reads the fee and never searches it: fee() at block-1, moved by FeeAdjustment(uint24,uint24) logs (topic 0x0cba8718, 117 groups) earlier in the block. It uses only the open price limit (MIN+1 or MAX-1), exact input with the logged paid amount or exact output with the logged received amount. The logged price may serve as the limit only when its bytes, without leading zeros, stand at a byte boundary in the transaction input. A pass 2 over the groups that failed pass 1 adds two values read from debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) of the swap's own transaction: the one word answer of the first STATICCALL that the pool's swap call makes to an address other than its two tokens (the fee the pool's code asked for), and the zeroForOne, amountSpecified and sqrtPriceLimitX96 arguments of the pool's own swap call. For every strict match that touched the branch, the same rerun was repeated with every 512 bit result of mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp replaced by result + 1. The swap counts as needing the branch when that rerun fails.
cleared.result: All 36,665 swaps that cycle 18 counted on the 512 bit branch match price, tick, liquidity, amount0 and amount1 to the unit under the strict rule (out/strict-final-summary.json). All 36,665 take the branch in their strict rerun (104,643 calls), and 31,044 fail when the branch result is made one unit wrong, so 31,044 swaps need src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 on 512 bit products to come out right. That is far more than the cycle 18 estimate of about 11,900. The reason is that the strict rerun cannot fall back on a limit set at the logged price. By factory: 0x07e60782 24,077 of 28,482, 0x32b9da73 3,405 of 3,460, 0xff7b3e8c 2,028 of 2,644, 0xb1c0fa0b 896 of 1,395, 0xecfa11c2 341 of 341, others 297 of 343. Modes: 32,427 exact input and 1,292 exact output with the fee from fee(), 2,792 with the fee read from the trace, 89 with the limit found in calldata, 65 with the arguments read from the trace. 28,516 of these had matched in cycle 18 only through the fee search or the limit at the logged price. Pass 1 matched 39,331 of the 39,752 swaps and failed 421, 406 of them on the branch. Pass 2 matched every one of the 421 (out/strict2.log, empty out/strict2.mismatch.jsonl). The causes all sit in the pools' own code. 341 are pools of factory 0xecfa11c2, for example 0x215aa7599bf881377cd2e8d03cd619ba3fe8eff8, whose swap asks fee contract 0x1d067a971008897baa4e0fb4fbd61cce985a12e8 (selector 0x0802f3f1) for the fee. That contract reads the HyperCore precompile 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000808, and the answers run from 1,500 to 33,872 pips while fee() answers 2,500. The other 80 are swaps whose router computes the price limit, for example the packed calldata of 0x0db606949817a021aad17dfdead276a5513dda0f13a88e52ad3a95d703bdb0c0, and the pool call's own limit reproduces them. The 3,460 swaps of the Slipstream style factory 0x32b9da73 match with the fee its swap reads from factory selector 0x35458dcc, which forwards to fee module 0x4992d95c (selector 0xb88c9148). That module answered 0 inside keeper transactions of 0x2d10ba71f994d20e5280e47eb9401a4f563e98af, after a call to its selector 0x51ac4e0b, and fee() answered 306 or 9. No swap is left without a match. Nothing points to validator MULMOD, DIV or comparison results that differ from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 or SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-252.

cleared.check: Task 2 (lead L-880), identification of the Algebra style pools. eth_call factory() on all 1,351 Swap emitters of the cycle 15 window (blocks 50,165,552 to 52,165,551) puts 127 pools and 937,210 swaps on the two factories: 0xf77bd082c627aa54591cf2f2eaa811fd1ab3b1f3 (74 pools, 663,167 swaps) and 0x5f95e92c338e6453111fc55ee66d4aafcce661a7 (53 pools, 274,043 swaps) (out/emitters.json, out/alg-sample.json). The plan names the second factory 0x5f95e92c338e6453111fc55ee66d4aa1df4e8e59, but eth_getCode returns no code at that address. The address with code, 10,699 bytes, is the one cycle 15 recorded. Neither pool bytecode is verified on Sourcify (v2 contract lookup for 0xbe512f58 and 0x12df9913 returns match null). The Routescan API answers 'chain not supported' and hyperscan.com redirects to another site, so the pools were identified from their bytecode instead. Their dispatcher selectors and PUSH32 event topics were compared with the interfaces of cryptoalgebra/Algebra at tags integral-v1.0, integral-v1.1 and integral-v1.2.2. Pools of 0xf77bd082 carry communityFeeLastTimestamp() and Fee(uint16) and lack the pluginFee getters, which is the Integral 1.0/1.1 interface. Pools of 0x5f95e92c carry lastFeeTransferTimestamp(), getPluginFeePending(), skim(), sync(), SwapFee(address,uint24,uint24) and BurnFee(address,uint24), which is the Integral 1.2.2 interface. Both emit the Uniswap v3 topics for Swap, Mint and Burn.
cleared.result: The swap step was taken from the tagged source and agrees with the reruns below. The tick table is a doubly linked list of initialized ticks: ticks(int24) returns liquidityTotal, liquidityDelta, prevTick and nextTick. prevTickGlobal and nextTickGlobal bracket the current tick, and a three layer bitmap tree is used only to find a neighbour on insertion (TickStructure._addOrRemoveTick, TickTree.getNextTick). The fee in pips is globalState.lastFee. On 1.0/1.1 it is changed by Fee(uint16) when the plugin calls setFee. On 1.2.2 the plugin's beforeSwap returns overrideFee and pluginFee, the fee is overrideFee + pluginFee when overrideFee is not 0 and lastFee + pluginFee otherwise, and SwapFee is logged just before Swap. The community fee and the plugin fee only split feeAmount after the step and change neither price nor amounts. PriceMovementMath.movePriceTowardsTarget is the v3 step with the input recomputed from the new price, and TokenDeltaMath.getToken0Delta/getToken1Delta and PriceMovementMath.getNewPrice equal SqrtPriceMath getAmount0Delta, getAmount1Delta, getNextSqrtPriceFromInput and getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput operation by operation. So the rerun uses tools/opdiff/v4math.py, the transcription of src/libraries.

cleared.check: Task 2, rerun of a seeded sample of the Algebra swaps (alg19.py). random.Random(19).sample of the 937,210 swaps, 20,000 swaps in 19,983 (pool, block) groups. All 22,560 swaps of those groups were rerun. Per group the collector reads eth_getLogs of the pool in the block, and at block-1 it reads globalState(), liquidity(), prevTickGlobal(), nextTickGlobal() and ticks(t) for each tick the loop reaches, all on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 at the start and end of each shard, 16:35:50 to 17:00:42 UTC). Mint and Burn logs earlier in the block are applied with TickManagement.update, the linked list insert and remove of TickStructure and the in-range rule of LiquidityMath.getAmountsForLiquidity. Fee and SwapFee logs set the fee as the source does. Limits are open, or the logged price when its bytes stand in the transaction input, or the swap or swapWithPaymentInAdvance call's own arguments read from debug_traceTransaction. Each rerun must equal price, tick, liquidity, amount0 and amount1 of the Swap log to the unit, and the fee is read, never searched.
cleared.result: 22,560 of 22,560 swaps reproduce to the unit, with 0 mismatches and 0 group errors (out/algB-summary.json). 16,330 are on 0xf77bd082 and 6,230 on 0x5f95e92c. Every 1.2.2 swap had a SwapFee log with a nonzero overrideFee and a pluginFee of 0. 20,835 swaps take one step and 1,725 several, and 1,779 cross an initialized tick. Modes: 17,349 exact input and 1,536 exact output with the open limit, 3,531 with the limit found in calldata, 144 with the pool call's own arguments from the trace. 3,846 swaps make 11,765 calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv, and 2,879 of them fail when that result is made one unit wrong. No swap reaches the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp. Pass 1 (out/alg-[0-3].*, without trace arguments) left 144 mismatches and 3 group errors, all saved in full in out/alg-*.mismatch.jsonl. Every one of the 144 fitted with the limit at the logged price while the limit bytes were absent from the input. The pool call's own limit from the trace reproduces each of them. The 3 errors came from a fault in the collector: the neighbour search walked the list from the wrong end when a minted tick lay outside [prevTickGlobal, nextTickGlobal]. Fixed, those groups reproduce. Mismatches left: none. The validator's arithmetic on this body agrees with src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116, SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-252 and TickMath.sol:57-237.

leads.question: Does any mined HyperEVM swap, in the v3 style or Algebra bodies outside the samples, reach the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-60) or an amount above 2^160, so that the closed validator's output on those branches can be checked as the 512 bit branch now is?
leads.why: After 36,665 strict v3 swaps and 22,560 Algebra swaps the 512 bit branch is measured, but the fallback branch still has no mined instance on the closed producer.

leadResults.answer: Under the strict rule (fee read from fee(), FeeAdjustment logs or the pool's own fee call in the trace; open limit, or a limit found in the calldata or in the pool call) all 36,665 swaps match to the unit. All take the 512 bit branch and 31,044 fail when its result is made one unit wrong. The 421 pass 1 failures come from a fee contract that reads HyperCore precompile 0x808 (341, factory 0xecfa11c2) and from router-computed limits (80). Each reproduces with the value the pool's own call used.

The two factories are Algebra Integral 1.0/1.1 (0xf77bd082) and 1.2.2 (0x5f95e92c...661a7). The collector reads globalState, liquidity, prevTickGlobal, nextTickGlobal and the tick linked list at the parent block and applies earlier Mint, Burn, Fee and SwapFee logs. All 22,560 swaps of the 19,983 sampled groups (seed 19, 20,000 swaps) reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit with the fee read. 3,846 reach the 512 bit branch (11,765 calls) and 2,879 need it. The MULMOD plant breaks 331 of 2,000 swaps and the TickMath plant 77.
